capitals.name: Bizye (Vize)
capitals.note: The Sapaeans 'ruled from their capital Bizye in what is now northwestern Turkey'; in 31 Bizye was already the Astaean seat ('with Bizye acting as the initial center'). No page names a capital for the Odrysian-Astaean kings of 87-31, so Bizye is carried back at confidence 1; Seuthopolis is listed only for c. 330-250 BC.

rulers.name: Cotys I (Sapaean)
rulers.note: Dynasty list of the Sapaean page; Cotys I ruled a Sapaean kingdom in the Rhodope before the house took all Thrace in 31.

rulers.name: Cotys III and Rhescuporis II (divided kingdom)

correction.text: the -87 shape without the land north of the Danube (Muntenia and Oltenia)

keyframe_review.note: 82,794 km2, bbox 23.15-28.64 E, 41.46-44.97 N: Bulgaria south of the Danube, the Edirne-Kirklareli corner of Turkish Thrace with Bizye, and Wallachia north of the river to 44.97 N. Even at its height the Odrysian kingdom ran 'from the Danube in the north to the outskirts of Abdera' (Sitalces), so the Wallachian third is removed. The Aegean coast (south of 41.46 N) is rightly absent: Macedonia province's border 'ran from Lissus on the Adriatic to the Hebrus River, which was the eastern border with Thrace'.

correction.text: the -42 shape without the land north of the Danube (Muntenia and Oltenia)

keyframe_review.note: 82,937 km2, a one-year shape differing from -87 by 143 km2; no page explains it (42 BC is Philippi, fought in Macedonia). Same Wallachian trim.

correction.text: the -41 shape without the land north of the Danube (Muntenia and Oltenia)

keyframe_review.note: 82,794 km2, identical to -87. Same trim. 31 BC: the Sapaeans replace the Odrysian-Astaean house (rename event), the kingdom is a Roman client from here (tint from the roman-republic dossier, then roman-empire).

correction.text: the -27 shape without the land north of the Danube (Muntenia and Oltenia)

keyframe_review.note: 90,345 km2, bbox 23.21-29.67 E, 41.46-45.56 N: 7,500 km2 added on the Black Sea coast up to the Danube delta (Dobruja) and more of Wallachia. Shortened to AD 5: 'Moesia was split off as a military command before 10 BC and became a province by AD 6' (Macedonia page), so the Danube bank is Roman from 6 (next keyframe). Wallachia removed as before; the delta coast is kept at confidence 1 as the only page statement is that the kingdom 'ruled much of Thrace'.

correction.text: the -27 shape without Wallachia and without Moesia, the Danube bank, a Roman province 'by AD 6'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Moesia 'became a province by AD 6'; the client kingdom keeps the land south of the Haemus. The AD 12 partition between Cotys III and Rhescuporis II ('the Romans divided his kingdom among his son Cotys III and his brother Rhescuporis II') is a division of the client kingship, not a border the pages draw.

correction.text: the -27 shape without Wallachia and Moesia

keyframe_review.note: 90,345 km2, drawn 43-50. Shortened to 46: 'In 46 AD, Roman Emperor Claudius put an end to the kingdom by annexing it' and 'made Thracia into a Roman province' (the Odrysian page: 'dissolved the Sapaean kingdom in 45/6'). Cliopatria's 50 has no event. The Macedonia page's 'AD 44, when the land between the Hebrus and Nestus was transferred to the new province of Thrace' is about the province's shape, not the kingdom's.

region.text: Thrace south of the Danube: the Haemus country, the Hebrus plain and the Bizye corner

ledger.note: 87 BC: the row begins. Cliopatria resumes the Thracian kingdom here, with the Odrysian row (odrysian-kingdom, -450..-338) ended 250 years earlier; the Odrysian page says Seuthes III 'revived a smaller Odrysian state around 330 BC' and that afterwards 'there is little conclusive evidence for the persistence of an Odrysian state'. The only page event in 87 is Macedonia's: 'From 87 BC, Thracian forces allied with Mithridates VI also attacked it'. Kept as a resume with no predecessor hand-over (confidence 1): the Odrysian-Astaean kings of Bizye whom Augustus removed in 31 are the house this row draws.

region.text: the Aegean coast of Macedonia province between the Strymon and the Hebrus

ledger.note: 87-85 BC: Thracian raids into Roman Macedonia with Mithridates. 'From 87 BC, Thracian forces allied with Mithridates VI also attacked' the province, whose eastern border was the Hebrus. The zone is the Aegean coast of the province; the end is Sulla's peace of 85 (First Mithridatic War page: Dardanos, 85).

region.text: the Aegean coast of Macedonia province between the Strymon and the Hebrus

ledger.note: 85 BC: the Mithridatic war ends with the Peace of Dardanos; the raids lapse on the pages.

31 BC: the Sapaean house takes the whole kingdom. 'Probably soon after the Battle of Actium in 31 BC, Roman leader Augustus sought to implement indirect rule over Thrace'; 'The Romans removed the Odrysian-Astaean royal family from power, and put the entire kingdom under Sapaean rule with Bizye acting as the initial center'. The Odrysian heartlands 'eventually became known as the Sapaean kingdom'; there is 'no evidence that Odrysians had any affiliations with the royal houses of the Sapaeans and Asti'. One row, one colour: the land and the seat are the same, the dynasty changes. Client status is drawn from the suzerain's side (roman-republic vassal_start 31, then roman-empire).

region.text: the Rhodope and Pirin mountains, the Bessi's country

ledger.counterpart: Bessi (Rhodope tribe under the priest Vologaesus)
ledger.note: 13-11 BC: the Bessi revolt. 'Around 13 BC, the Bessi under a priest named Vologaesus revolted and killed the Thracian king'; 'A separate, unsuccessful revolt followed in 11 BC'. Zone: the Rhodope, the Bessi's mountains.

region.text: the Rhodope and Pirin mountains, the Bessi's country

ledger.counterpart: Bessi (Rhodope tribe under the priest Vologaesus)
ledger.note: 11 BC: the second Bessi rising fails; 'Roman expansion along the Danube followed the Bessi revolt'.

region.text: the Danube bank between the Haemus and the river (Moesia Inferior)

ledger.note: AD 6: Moesia a Roman province. 'Moesia was split off as a military command before 10 BC and became a province by AD 6' (Macedonia page). Whether the Danube bank was ever the client kings' land is not said on the pages; it is removed here so that Roman Moesia and the kingdom do not overlap. Confidence 1.
AD 21: the Odrysian rising. 'Rhoemetalces II took refuge in Philippopolis in AD 21 during a rebellion that included Odrysians, which failed.'
AD 21: the rebellion 'failed' within the year.

region.text: the kingdom south of the Haemus

ledger.note: AD 44-46: the last revolt. 'Around 44/45 AD, another revolt broke out during which king Rhoemetalces III was killed' (his reign is listed 38-46).
AD 46: Claudius ends the revolt and the kingdom together.

region.text: the whole client kingdom, the province of Thracia

ledger.note: AD 46: 'In 46 AD, Roman Emperor Claudius put an end to the kingdom by annexing it' and 'made Thracia into a Roman province'; the Odrysian page: 'The Romans dissolved the Sapaean kingdom in 45/6 and made it the province of Thracia'. Cliopatria's row runs to 50 with no event.

certainty.note: A client kingdom of tribes under a Hellenized court: the Haemus, the Danube and the Hebrus are the only lines the pages name. The Bizye corner is the one firm part; the Rhodope (Bessi) and the Black Sea coast to the delta are the softest. The pre-31 Odrysian-Astaean extent is taken from Cliopatria at confidence 1.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Thracian Kingdom' row (-87..50, 5 shapes) has no article of its own ('Thracian kingdom' is a disambiguation page listing the Odrysian kingdom c. 480-30 BC, Lysimachus' kingdom and the Sapaean kingdom); the row is the late Odrysian-Astaean kingdom of Bizye and, from 31 BC, the Sapaean client kingdom, drawn as one state with a dynastic rename in 31. Identity.wikipedia is set to 'Sapaean kingdom' (the only article covering the Roman-client phase) and the seed's wikidata Q104815700 is kept unverified. Start 87 is Cliopatria's and is kept (confidence 1): no page gives a foundation, the Odrysian page doubts the state's continuity after Seuthes III, and the only 87 event is the Thracian attack on Macedonia with Mithridates. End moved from 50 to 46 (Claudius' annexation, both pages). Shapes: all five include Wallachia north of the Danube (to 44.97/45.56 N), removed throughout since even Sitalces' kingdom stopped at the Danube; the -27 shape adds the Dobruja coast to the delta (kept, confidence 1); Moesia is removed from AD 6 (new keyframe) when it 'became a province by AD 6'. The Aegean coast is rightly absent (Roman Macedonia to the Hebrus). The rulers list follows the Sapaean page's dynasty list with its own overlaps (Rhescuporis I 48-41 and Cotys II 42-15 overlap in 42-41; Rhoemetalces II's start is the end of the AD 12-19 division, the page gives no year, so 19 is a placeholder; Rhoemetalces III 38-46 'overlaps the death date' 44/45). Client status (tint) is drawn from the suzerain's dossiers: roman-republic vassal_start 31 (month 9); the roman-empire dossier should carry vassal_start thracian-kingdom at -27 (or -30) and vassal_end 46. Counterparts without dossiers: the Bessi, the AD 21 and AD 44 rebels (text strings). Gazetteer gaps: Bizye/Vize (circle used), Rhodope and Haemus (admin1 unions used), Seuthopolis, Philippopolis as a place (admin1 Plovdiv used).
